The robot controller's state updates are missing or too old, so the motion or Stop could not be confirmed. Check the robot connection and its driver component.
The cell changed between reading its state and sending this request. Review the current state and try again.

column2: Gripper changed during Stop or Reset
column3: The gripper command changed while a Stop or Reset was applied to it, so the request was refused. Check the gripper before continuing.
A process or remote resource of a previous launch may still be running, so the launcher refused to continue. Stop the previous launch first.
The request was addressed to an earlier run of the service, which has restarted since. Refresh the view and try again.
The Scene changed after this request was prepared, so the request was refused. Refresh the Scene and try again.
The robot is not where the planned motion starts.
The launcher could not read or write its launch status record.
A position Reset step did not finish within its time limit and the position Reset was closed. Check the arm state and run the position Reset again.
An internal check failed: a Stop stage asked for evidence the robot interface cannot provide. Collect the logs and report it.

column2: Stop did not finish braking in time
column3: The robot was not confirmed stopped within the Stop time limit. Check the robot; the cell needs Recover before further motion.
An internal check failed: a prepared motion carried an invalid Stop evidence requirement. Collect the logs and report it.

column2: Stop stage has no evidence contract
column3: An internal check failed: a Stop stage has no evidence requirements. Collect the logs and report it.

column2: Stop evidence came from another source
column3: The Stop could not be confirmed because its evidence did not come from the expected robot connection, for example after the controller reconnected. Check the robot; the cell needs Recover before further motion.
The Stop could not be confirmed because the robot state used as evidence was too old. Check the robot and its connection; the cell needs Recover before further motion.
The Stop could not be confirmed. Use the safety controller and check the robot.

column2: A newer cell Stop replaced this one
column3: A newer cell Stop replaced the one this Recover cell press saw. Press Recover cell again.
The cell refused to recover from the Stop. Check the cell state and the details, then press Recover cell again.
The cell Stop cannot be recovered right now; the details give the reason.
The Stop ramp ended with the robot outside the controller's goal tolerance, so the Stop is not confirmed settled and intervention is required. Check the robot before recovering.

column2: Stop record conflicts with its plan
column3: An internal check failed: a saved Stop record conflicts with its Stop plan. Collect the logs and report it.
The controlled Stop duration must be greater than 0 and at most 2 seconds. Correct the Stop duration.
An internal check failed: the saved Stop record state is invalid. Collect the logs and report it.

column2: Stop stage superseded by a newer Stop
column3: A newer Stop superseded this Stop stage after it had been sent to the robot.

column2: Waiting for a fresh robot sample after Stop
column3: After the Stop, the robot state source has not yet produced a fresh sample to confirm the robot is at rest.

column2: Stop result does not match its scope
column3: An internal check failed: a Stop stage result does not match its Stop scope or plan. Collect the logs and report it.
An internal check failed: a Stop stage has more than one final result. Collect the logs and report it.

column2: Cancelled Stop stage has a result
column3: An internal check failed: a Stop stage cancelled before sending also carries a result. Collect the logs and report it.
An internal check failed: Stop evidence exceeded its size limit. Collect the logs and report it.
An internal check failed: Stop evidence contains conflicting duplicate entries. Collect the logs and report it.
An internal check failed: a Stop stage has more than one late superseded result. Collect the logs and report it.
An internal check failed: a stored or exchanged record holds a non-text value where text is required. Collect the logs and report it.
An internal check failed: a prepared operation contains an invalid interrupt value. Collect the logs and report it.
An internal check failed: a prepared operation contains invalid interrupt values. Collect the logs and report it.
A newer runtime configuration replaced the one this request was for, so it was refused.
The expression is too large. Simplify it.
A TCP pose has invalid or non-finite values. Correct the TCP definition.
Choose the TCP for each listed move.
The request names its TCP in the format of an older ManyForge version. Open the Program in the Composer, save it and Apply it again.
Two TCPs have the same name. Give each TCP its own name.
The robot controller did not apply the TCP offset.
A TCP names a parent link the model does not have. Correct the TCP definition.
An internal check failed: a TCP selection in a request is malformed. Collect the logs and report it.

column2: Tool not mounted on this robot
column3: The TCP belongs to a tool that is not mounted on this robot, so it was refused before anything moved. Mount the tool on this robot or choose another TCP.
The stopped motion is still finishing its cleanup, so Resume, Retry and Close are not available yet. Try again in a moment.
An internal check failed: the result of the component start could not be recorded. The Apply was stopped. Collect the logs and report it.
The pose source could not look up the configured transform. Check that the frames exist and the transform is published.
The expression is too long. Simplify it.

A motion that takes over a moving robot names a different TCP than the running motion. The TCP is never changed during motion, so the takeover was refused. Let the current motion finish, then start the motion again.

column2: Tool frame not fixed to the flange
column3: The TCP or attachment frame is not rigidly fixed to the robot flange, so the robot's tool settings could not be built. Choose a frame on the robot flange or a mounted tool.
An attachment uses a frame that neither the robot nor its mounted tools have. Check the attachment and the tool mounting.

column2: Tool settings not sent to the robot
column3: The robot's TCP and payload for this motion could not be sent to its controller, so the motion was refused before it started. Check the robot connection and try again.
Only a pneumatic gripper tool may leave out its Mock, Sim and Real controller profiles. Add the controller profile to the tool, or author its gripper as pneumatic.

column2: Pneumatic tool has no I/O outputs
column3: A commanded pneumatic tool without a controller profile needs its pneumatic I/O outputs. Add the pneumatic I/O to the tool's gripper settings.

column2: Robot did not follow the path
column3: The robot deviated from the planned path or final position by more than the allowed tolerance, so the motion was aborted. Check the robot and its surroundings before running again.
An internal check failed: the straight-path accuracy metrics of a trajectory are invalid. Collect the logs and report it.
An internal check failed: the waypoint times of a straight-path trajectory are missing or invalid. Collect the logs and report it.
An internal check failed: a trajectory has an empty, duplicate or mismatched joint list. Collect the logs and report it.
An internal check failed: a trajectory contains a non-finite number or times that do not increase. Collect the logs and report it.
An internal check failed: the speed-scaling bounds of a trajectory are invalid. Collect the logs and report it.
An internal check failed: a speed-scalable trajectory lacks velocities or accelerations for every joint. Collect the logs and report it.

column2: Trajectory must start and end at rest
column3: An internal check failed: a speed-scalable trajectory does not start or end at rest. Collect the logs and report it.
An internal check failed: the recorded validation metrics of a trajectory are invalid. Collect the logs and report it.
An internal check failed: a trajectory waypoint does not have one value per joint. Collect the logs and report it.
An internal check failed: a trajectory record has no waypoint list. Collect the logs and report it.
An internal limit was reached: no further lifecycle steps can be numbered. Collect the logs and report it.
An internal check failed: the trusted sign-in adapter returned an incomplete user identity. Collect the logs and report it.
Motion is blocked by unacknowledged alarms. Acknowledge them, then try again.
The expression is empty or ends too early. Complete the expression.
The expression contains an unexpected symbol. Correct the expression.
The expression calls a function that does not exist. Correct the expression.
An internal check failed: a stored or exchanged record has unknown or missing fields. Collect the logs and report it.
An internal check failed: a prepared motion still names a target that should have been resolved to a position. Collect the logs and report it.
The selected robot or component does not offer this capability.
A string in the expression is not closed with a double quote. Correct the expression.

column2: AI model server returned an error
column3: The AI model server answered with an HTTP error. Check the AI model server.
The AI model server reply is not in the expected format.
The AI model server reply exceeded its size limit and was dropped.
The AI model server did not answer in time. Check the server load and try again.
The AI model server could not be reached. Check that it is running and reachable.
The planned motion would collide.
The motion could not be validated yet.
The motion exceeds a joint, speed or acceleration limit.
An internal check failed: the validation version recorded with a motion is not valid. Collect the logs and report it.
An internal check failed: the robot model data for the 3D view is inconsistent or out of bounds. Collect the logs and report it.
This execution host has no motion trace collector, or the trace could not be captured within its size limit.
An internal check failed: a request to the 3D viewer worker was built with invalid fields. Collect the logs and report it.
The data for the 3D viewer worker exceeded its size limit and was not sent. Collect the logs and report it.
An internal check failed: the 3D viewer worker returned a malformed or corrupted reply. Collect the logs and report it.
The motion controller is shutting down its motion worker, so the request was refused. Wait for the lifecycle step to finish and try again.

column2: Component start could not be scheduled
column3: An internal check failed: the component start work could not be scheduled. The Apply was stopped. Collect the logs and report it.
A function in the expression is called with the wrong number of arguments. Correct the expression.

column2: Robot axes not enabled: use Recover cell
column3: The robot was moved from its own interface and not all of its axes are enabled, so ManyForge cannot re-engage it and the motion was not started. Use Recover cell, then start the motion again.

column2: Robot reports an error: use Recover cell
column3: The robot was moved from its own interface and now reports an error (for example after an emergency stop), so ManyForge does not re-engage it automatically and the motion was not started. Clear the cause, then use Recover cell.
The robot's reported or measured joint angles are missing or invalid, so the robot controller was not activated. Check the robot connection and the xArm controller, then activate again.
A measured joint angle differs from the angle the xArm controller reports, so the robot controller was not activated. Check the robot and its joint readings, then activate again.

column2: Robot still moving under its own control
column3: The robot is still moving under its own interface, so ManyForge cannot re-engage it and the motion was not started. Wait until the robot stops, then start the motion again.

column2: Robot not armed: use Recover cell
column3: The robot was moved from its own interface and is not armed, so ManyForge cannot re-engage it and the motion was not started. Use Recover cell, then start the motion again.

The xArm controller is not ready for commands (error, mode, state or motors not enabled), so the robot controller was not activated. Clear the robot error and enable it with Prepare or Recover, then activate again.

The robot did not confirm a step of its re-engage (its mode or state change, or the state change after a TCP offset), so the motion was not started. Check the robot and its connection, then start the motion again; if it repeats, use Recover cell.

After its re-engage the robot did not report joint-servo mode and the ready state in time, so the motion was not started. Check the robot, then start the motion again; if it repeats, use Recover cell.

The xArm controller's status report is missing or out of date, or the xArm connection is not started, so the robot controller was not activated. Check the robot connection and that the xArm driver is running.
